title: Dual scalar comparisons of lines and signed tensor and tower coherence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with finite limits and final object, small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R_0\xrightarrow{\iota_{01}}R_1\xrightarrow{\iota_{12}}R_2$ be commutative ring sheaves and $\iota_{02}=\iota_{12}\iota_{01}$. Let $L_i$ be $R_i$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], each locally isomorphic to $R_i$ on a covering of the final object. Suppose given isomorphisms $b_{ij}:L_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}L_j$ for $i<j$, with $b_{02}=b_{12}(b_{01}\otimes1)$ under tensor reassociation. Use sheaf tensor and sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom], and write $L_i^{[0]}=R_i$, $L_i^{[n]}=L_i^{\otimes n}$ and $L_i^{[-n]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[n]},R_i)$ for $n>0$. For $m\geq0$ let $b_{ij,m}$ be the unit and recursively induced tensor-power comparisons of $b_{ij}$. For $n>0$ the formula
$$\beta_{ij,n}(\varphi\otimes s)(x\otimes t)=\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st$$
defines an isomorphism
$$\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[n]},R_i)\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{R_j}(L_i^{[n]}\otimes_{R_i}R_j,R_j).$$
Set $b_{ij,-n}(\varphi\otimes s)=\beta_{ij,n}(\varphi\otimes s)\circ b_{ij,n}^{-1}$. These signed-power isomorphisms commute with evaluation, in the precise sense
$$\operatorname{ev}(b_{ij,-n}(\varphi\otimes s),b_{ij,n}(x\otimes t))=\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st.$$
For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\mu_i^{a,b}:L_i^{[a]}\otimes_{R_i}L_i^{[b]}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i^{[a+b]}$, normalized by $e_i^a\otimes e_i^b\mapsto e_i^{a+b}$ for every local basis $e_i$ of $L_i$; negative powers of a basis mean its dual powers. It is the map given by tensor associativity, symmetry and evaluation contractions. If $\sigma_{ij}$ is the canonical scalar/tensor comparison, then
$$b_{ij,a+b}\circ(\mu_i^{a,b}\otimes1)=\mu_j^{a,b}\circ(b_{ij,a}\otimes b_{ij,b})\circ\sigma_{ij}.$$
For every integer $m$, the maps satisfy
$$b_{02,m}\circ\mathrm{ass}=b_{12,m}\circ(b_{01,m}\otimes1),$$
where $\mathrm{ass}:((M\otimes_{R_0}R_1)\otimes_{R_1}R_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_{R_0}R_2$ sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes\iota_{12}(s)t$ and has inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. For identity ring maps equipped with the multiplication comparison at exponent one, every $b_{ii,m}$ is the tensor-unit comparison. On any compatible local bases $e_j=b_{ij}(e_i\otimes1)$ the formula for every signed exponent is $b_{ij,m}((r e_i^m)\otimes s)=\iota_{ij}(r)s e_j^m$.

proof.text: Construct each positive basis recursively with the actual sheaf tensor, starting with 1 in degree zero. Restriction of the tensor to a slice and its unitors show that these elements are bases on every further slice. Define the negative basis using the inverse of the positive basis chart, viewed as the localDual section of the slice internal Hom. Evaluation on the positive basis is 1. The existing localDual_coordinates theorem expresses every functional in this dual basis; together with evaluation this proves bijectivity and uniqueness of the full signed basis family.

Positive tensor powers are locally the unit by induction and localized tensor restriction. Their IsInvertible instances therefore follow from the given cover. Apply scalarExtensionDual_localIsomorphism to these powers to prove that the canonical scalarExtensionDualMap is invertible. This proves the signedLineDual_isIso clause without flatness.

Construct positive comparison isomorphisms recursively from scalarExtensionUnitIso, the given degree-one comparison, and scalarTensorBinaryIso. For negative degrees compose asIso of the proved dual map with precomposition by the inverse positive comparison. Its inverse is precomposition by the forward comparison. The normalization is definitional. Evaluation cancels the inverse positive comparison and scalarExtensionDualMap_tmul gives the displayed formula. For the basis formula induct on positive powers, then evaluate a negative functional on the target positive basis; its coordinates determine the functional. The scalar balancing formula supplies arbitrary coefficients.

Construct local products with basisChart: the tensor of the degree-a and degree-b generators is a basis by tensorBasis_bijective, and its chart composed with the degree-(a+b) chart gives an isomorphism on each slice. For two normalized signed basis families E and F, expand F_1=r E_1 and E_1=s F_1; injectivity gives sr=rs=1, including for the zero ring. Form the unit t=(r,s). Induction and tensor bilinearity give F_n=t^n E_n for nonnegative n; evaluate negative functionals on E_n and use t^(-n)t^n=1 to obtain the same formula for every integer. The identity t^(a+b)=t^a t^b proves that every local product sends every normalized signed basis tensor to the corresponding sum-degree basis, hence that the chart maps agree on every common restriction. Glue their sections in the actual internal Hom sheaf using the CoversTop section-gluing theorem, and convert the resulting global section to a module morphism. Its components are bijective wherever a map to a cover member exists, so local bijectivity and reflection of isomorphisms by the underlying-sheaf functor make it an isomorphism. Sheaf separation extends normalization to arbitrary local bases. Finally, restrict any competing normalized product to the chosen cover and expand every tensor section in its tensor basis; linearity gives equality on all sections, so the product is unique.

Transport a source basis e through the exponent-one comparison. Apply the existing extendedBasisIso from the scalar dual local-isomorphism module to its basis chart. Its inverse sends a scalar r to scalarExtensionSection alpha L r e, and the exponent-one comparison carries this isomorphism to the target. Naturality identifies its unit generator with the restriction of the transported section. Thus that section is a basis after every restriction; construct its signed powers. Test the tensor square on scalar-extended pure tensors and restrict to the source basis cover. Expand both sections in signed bases. Product normalization and the comparison basis formula identify the coefficients by multiplicativity and commutativity.

Use the existing scalarExtensionTowerIso with its pure-section formula. Propagate a source basis through the first and second exponent-one comparisons using the preceding extended-basis isomorphism argument. The exponent-one tower hypothesis identifies this final basis with the direct comparison. In each signed degree, expand a source section as z times the source basis. The two routes on an iterated pure section have coefficients beta(alpha(z))*(t*beta(s)) and beta(alpha(z)*s)*t. These agree by multiplicativity and commutativity. Iterated scalar-extension generation and sheaf separation prove the tower equation.

For an identity coefficient map with multiplication in degree one, the basis is compatible with itself. Apply the signed comparison basis formula on a trivializing cover and expand an arbitrary source section as r times that basis. Both sides have coefficient r*s=s*r. Naturality and sheaf separation give the identity formula globally in every signed degree.

split_report.summary: Expanded every signed comparison and tensor/tower equation in local bases. Reused the existing sheaf tensor universal property, localized restriction, Hom gluing, normalized binary scalar comparison and scalar dual evaluation. No statement correction and no new nodes; all signs, non-flat maps and units are covered.
split_report.blueprint: prop-weil-twist-preserves.proof.md: the sentence that twists are tensor powers and internal Homs, and the last sentence about levelwise and common finite stages. Steps 2-7 construct signed comparisons and contractions, step 8 checks tensor compatibility, steps 9-10 give coefficient towers and identities.

tool_uses.why: Uses only the ordinary sheaf tensor bilinear universal property to construct and compare the local pairings and balanced coefficient associator; the unit has no such universal-property node.
Uses restriction of the actual sheaf tensor to arbitrary localized sites, preserving pure sections, to compute on a basis cover; this is generic sheaf infrastructure absent from the unit.
Uses existence and uniqueness of gluing linear maps on one cover, both for basis-independent products and inverse maps; this generic locality theorem is not a step replacing the unit route.

Uses only normalized binary tensor, unit and scalar comparisons, with their section formulas, to induce positive powers and compute the tensor square; the signed powers and tower equalities are proved here.
Uses the canonical ordinary dual evaluation map and its section formula, not any signed-power or tower assertion; its rank-one inverse is proved here.
